name: synapse-packing-stress-v1
purpose: Larger paraphrase-heavy synthetic fixture with two judged relevant memories per query, designed to study candidate recall versus context-packing retention. Deterministic embeddings are lexical-like and non-semantic; results are not a semantic retrieval benchmark.

documents.content: A release is eligible for publication only after a signed version tag is pushed to the canonical repository.
The publish gate checks package metadata and requires the integration suite to pass before any artifact is uploaded.
An encrypted snapshot can be restored only with the exact data encryption key that protected the original records.
Key rotation is complete only after retained records have been re-encrypted and decryption has been verified with the new key.
Changing the embedding model changes the vector space, so old vectors are not directly comparable to newly generated vectors.
After changing the embedding output width, every stored memory must be re-embedded before new queries use the index.
Every request must bind a validated tenant identity before any memory read or mutation is allowed.
PostgreSQL row-level security denies records when the active session tenant is missing or conflicts with the requested tenant.
A client receiving throttling should use the Retry-After guidance and apply bounded exponential backoff.
Redis-backed request counters coordinate rate limits across multiple engine replicas instead of limiting each process independently.
A deletion request must remove the original memory from the active store and prevent it from being returned by later queries.
Deletion verification must also cover searchable projections and indexes derived from the original content.
Context assembly must never exceed the configured token allowance merely to include another high-ranked memory.
Memory selection should be evaluated by relevant facts retained per token, not just the sum of raw ranking scores.
Readiness should report success only when the configured storage backend can serve requests.
Liveness only proves the process is running; it must not be treated as proof that PostgreSQL is accepting queries.
HTTP request traces include a correlation ID so operators can follow a single request through the gateway.
The application connection pool defaults to twelve concurrent database connections per process.
The HNSW graph uses a neighbor parameter of sixteen for the current default index configuration.
Transient worker failures use exponential retries with a maximum of five attempts.
A successful deployment records the container image digest in the release manifest.
The background compaction task is scheduled once per day during the low-traffic window.
API credentials and data encryption credentials are distinct secrets with separate rotation procedures.
The gateway exports request counts, status codes, and duration histograms to the metrics endpoint.
Database migration output is retained in the deployment log for incident diagnosis.
The local development server binds to loopback by default to avoid accidental network exposure.
Batch ingestion caps each HTTP payload to keep memory use predictable during import.
A cache entry is revalidated after its configured time-to-live elapses.
The job queue records failed tasks for later inspection by the service owner.
The service rejects unknown request fields when strict input validation is enabled.
The API schema is available from the local OpenAPI endpoint when documentation is enabled.
The deployment pipeline captures image scan summaries before publishing deployment metadata.
When profile notes conflict, the latest explicit user preference takes precedence over older saved entries.
Older profile notes may remain as history but should be clearly marked as superseded when a newer preference exists.
Eligible refund requests must be submitted within thirty calendar days of purchase.
A refund is eligible only when the customer supplies a receipt that identifies the original transaction.
Before escalating a payment outage, support should confirm that the service health alert is active.
A confirmed payment-processing outage should be handed to the on-call engineer with the incident ID and impact summary.
Priority-one tickets have a fifteen-minute initial-response target during staffed support hours.
The staffed support window runs Monday through Friday, from 09:00 to 18:00 UTC.
A verified privacy erasure request must remove the customer's personal information from active searchable memory.
The erasure workflow records a non-sensitive audit event after deletion is verified across the primary store and derived indexes.
An account recovery request must pass identity verification before a reset link is issued.
Password reset links expire after twenty minutes and can be consumed only once.
When two support cases describe the same incident, link the duplicate to the canonical case instead of replying independently.
Every open support case must have a named owner responsible for the next customer update.
Customer identifiers should be redacted from general application logs unless access is explicitly authorized.
A shift handoff should include current status, actions already taken, and the next expected update.
The customer portal displays the current severity label next to each active support case.
Billing questions are assigned to the revenue operations queue when they do not require engineering.
Feature requests receive a response within three business days when submitted through the feedback portal.
The knowledge base article ID is included in support replies when a self-service guide is available.
Agents should attach the browser version when reporting a reproducible user-interface issue.
The standard onboarding package includes two remote configuration sessions.
The support portal groups open cases by organization and severity.
A reopened issue is returned to the previous queue unless its product area has changed.
Administrative console access requires a second factor in addition to the account password.
The weekly support report counts incoming cases, solved cases, and median time to close.
Agents may request a screen recording when written reproduction steps are insufficient.
Trial extension requests are reviewed by the account team before any contract dates are modified.
Customer satisfaction surveys are sent after a case is marked resolved.
The escalation channel uses a template containing service, severity, and customer impact.
Production impersonation sessions are time-limited and recorded for audit.
The support dashboard refreshes queue totals every sixty seconds.
The quarterly pipeline review starts at 14:00 UTC on the final Friday of each quarter.
Account owners must update forecast amounts and explain material changes before the pipeline review begins.
EMEA opportunities are grouped by country and expected closing quarter for regional analysis.
Regional forecasts distinguish committed revenue from upside opportunities that still need buyer confirmation.
Every opportunity record requires an account owner, expected close date, and current deal stage.
A deal may advance to the negotiation stage only after the buyer's requirements and decision process are documented.
Closed-account sales notes are retained for twenty-four months unless a contractual rule requires less.
At the end of the allowed retention period, records are deleted from the active account history and its searchable copies.
Discounts above fifteen percent require written approval from the regional sales director.
A proposed discount must keep the deal above the approved margin floor unless finance grants an exception.
Commission calculations are checked against the final signed contract value before payout.
A post-signature price change must be reflected in the commission record before the next payout cycle.
Partner-sourced opportunities must record the referring partner before they enter the qualified pipeline.
When a channel partner shares ownership of a deal, the agreed revenue split must be attached to the opportunity.
Each active opportunity is assigned to one primary territory owner who coordinates the next customer action.
Territory reassignment requires an accepted handoff with the next action and target date.
The sales dashboard refreshes regional totals every thirty minutes during business hours.
New leads are routed according to industry, company size, and assigned territory.
The standard introductory call is scheduled for twenty-five minutes.
The weekly sales digest lists new opportunities and deals that have changed stage.
Sales representatives should log the meeting outcome on the account record before the end of the day.
The product demonstration environment resets its sample data every Monday morning.
Travel expenses must be submitted before the monthly finance close.
The account plan includes stakeholders, renewal date, business goals, and expansion risks.
The standard proposal template contains commercial terms and a customer signature page.
A closed-lost deal may be reopened when new buyer evidence changes the qualification assessment.
Customer references require written permission from the account owner.
The forecasting dashboard distinguishes new business from existing-customer expansion.
A sales engineer joins technical discovery when the prospect requires a non-standard integration.
The regional team maintains a shared calendar for major industry events.
Company-branded gifts above the stated threshold require compliance review.
The monthly report lists overdue follow-ups and opportunities without a recent activity note.

queries.query: What needs to be in place before software can be shipped, and what blocks its publication?
How can protected snapshots be recovered, and when is credential rotation truly finished?
What preparation is needed when the vector representation changes its model or width?
How do concurrent requests keep one customer's saved context from leaking to another?
When clients are throttled, how should they recover and how is rate control shared across replicas?
What must be verified before claiming that a memory removal request is complete?
How should retrieval context stay within a strict allowance while preserving useful facts?
What do service health signals tell us when the process is alive but storage may be down?
When a person's saved instructions disagree, which version should be used and what happens to the old note?
What evidence and timing determine whether a purchase can be reimbursed?
What should support confirm and include before handing a payment incident to engineering?
How quickly must the most urgent cases be answered, and when does that target apply?
How is a verified customer erasure request carried through, and how is completion recorded?
What checks protect account recovery, and how long is the one-time reset link usable?
How should duplicate incident reports and ownership of the next update be handled?
What safeguards limit exposure of customer identifiers and preserve a clean shift handoff?
When does the pipeline review occur, and what preparation is required from each owner?
How are regional opportunities grouped, and how is firm revenue distinguished from upside?
What details must be present on a deal, and what evidence allows it to progress?
How long may closed-account notes remain, and what happens after that period ends?
What approvals and financial guardrails apply when a representative proposes a large discount?
What must be checked before commission payout and after contract value changes?
What attribution and commercial agreement details are needed for a partner-led deal?
Who coordinates next steps on an opportunity, and what is required when ownership changes?
